meta.title: Otra Gran Torre Costanera, en Puente Alto
meta.question: ¿Qué pasaría si copiamos la Gran Torre Costanera en Puente Alto, con sus empleos?
meta.analyze: Cómo crece el movimiento de la mañana alrededor de la torre nueva, de 06:00 a 09:00.

cues.caption: Copiamos la Gran Torre Costanera en Puente Alto, con 5.863 empleos.
Son las 6 de la mañana. Miremos cómo despierta la comuna.
Las calles se llenan: 5.779 personas trabajan ahora en la torre.
2.720 de ellas viven en Puente Alto. Ya no cruzan la ciudad.
Al Metro Plaza de Puente Alto: 4.413 entradas diarias más, según el modelo.
En toda la ciudad, 7.191 trabajadores cambian de lugar de trabajo.

assumptions: Persons are synthetic and consistent with the Census 2024 margins. They are not microdata.
The station model (L9) is fitted on the baseline. Its scale, classes and profiles do not change.
Travel times are comuna to comuna and lower than survey times. The effect of a time change is an unvalidated sensitivity; the size and direction of its error are unknown.
Stations use the baseline public share of the home comuna, scaled by the change in its public-transport workers.
Open city for residents: more or fewer residents change the total of workers, with the baseline workers per resident of the comuna.
Station access (L9): a walk within 1,000 m, or else one bus. A closed station does not change the travel minutes between comunas or the job choice.
Trips are display groups of workers, not persons. Departure half hours come from the EOD 2012 survey. Students are not included.

The Census sets walking and cycling totals inside each comuna pair. The 2012 survey distance rule allocates workers within those totals. The engine has no measured response for cycling uptake after a new cycleway.
All values are model values, not measured values.

When a mode loses places, who keeps it is a deterministic weighted draw: the weight is the Census 2024 share of that mode among workers of the same home comuna, age band and household size. Unknown household size has its own group for the draw. These workers count in age summaries only. mode_change_by_person follows from this rule, not from an observed response. Workers that a residents change adds are not counted.
The scenario supplies the building job count.
The scenario supplies the building resident count.

Known stocks use uniform density over the footprint's covered census-block area. Shares sum to one across covered area; street gaps receive no stock. Scalar block metadata and any occupancy rate use the largest-area block.

health.unit: weekday outbound health trips of residents (EOD 2012 rates × Census 2024 residents), not distinct persons; returns are not included. shops_* count the destination points of health_points.csv

optional_visits.unit: persons who make an optional weekday shopping visit (workers and other residents); trips = persons × 1.608 (EOD 2012 trips per shopper)

workers_by_household_income_band.cash: Illustrative daily round trip, 2026 CLP, same mode out and back: public 2 × 795 (Red bus with transfers); car, fuel-only proxy, 2 × engine comuna-pair km × 1,414 CLP/l (CNE RM gasoline 93, Sep 2026) ÷ 16.9 km/Lge (ICCT, 2025 new light vehicles of all technologies, assumed for a gasoline commuter car); walk and bicycle 0. Engine km is straight-line between comuna points (same comuna: half the distance to the nearest other comuna), not a measured trip distance. Parking, tolls and Metro peak fares (+100) are not included. Taxi/colectivo and other modes have no price and are counted as unpriced.
workers_by_household_income_band.unit: workers (synthetic persons with a modeled work trip); pct = count / workers in the band. Band = imputed CASEN 2024 monthly household monetary income, November 2024 CLP, drawn from the CASEN workers of the home comuna (commune is not a CASEN survey domain). Unmodeled: unknown private household or age outside the source.

population.source: workers: Census 2024 internal commuters (mode_od.csv); students: MINEDUC 2026 enrollment (school_od.csv) plus 69.6 % of Census higher-education residents, placed at SIES 2026 campuses by in-person + hybrid registrations and travel time from the home comuna, with the work destination beta (higher_ed.csv, choice.rs; assumption: students weigh time like workers); the 69.6 % is the in-person + hybrid share of registrations, used as the weekday travel share: an unverified assumption, not a measured attendance; other_residents: Census 2024 persons who are neither an internal commuter nor attend basic or secondary school (Census attendance, person_traits_residents.csv). The MINEDUC student count and the Census exclusion cover different school levels, and a commuting student can count as both a worker and a student, so the three groups can overlap. Other residents have a home and traits; their only modeled trip is the optional shopping visit (optional_visits).

shopping.unit: weekday outbound shopping trips of residents (EOD 2012 rates × Census 2024 residents), not distinct persons; returns are not included. shops_* count the destination points of activity_points.csv shop, mall, supermarket

worksite_cohorts.name: Gran Torre Costanera
worksite_cohorts.scope: A typical weekday. Counts follow synthetic workers assigned to this exact scenario worksite. Outside means the modeled home comuna differs from the placed building's primary census-block comuna.
worksite_cohorts.time_scope: Travel times are comuna-pair proxies for the same assigned workers. Car uses the scenario road graph at free flow between comuna anchors. Public uses the morning GTFS pair table and scheduled route times from full-day transit edits. Behavioral time assumptions and imputed distance-fit pairs do not supply route times. Timed transit scenarios have no public-travel times in this result. The Census public category includes bus, Metro, train, taxi and colectivo. The time proxy uses scheduled transit. Other modes and local journeys have no time in this result. These are not door-to-door times to the building.
